title: Even Tabassum cried
takeaway: Even someone whose name means 'smile' can be brought to tears.
scene: A short Urdu poem titled 'An expression of grief', written for Gulzar-e-Naz, who died on 16 January 1986.

original: غم کے ہر ایک اشک کو مژگاں میں پرونا آیا
دل کے دکھ درد کو آہوں میں سمونا آیا
transliteration: Gham ke har ek ashk ko mizhgaan mein pirona aaya
Dil ke dukh dard ko aahon mein samona aaya
translation: I learned to thread every tear of grief onto my eyelashes;
I learned to fold the heart's pain into my sighs.
couplets.story: He has learned to string his tears along his eyelashes like beads, and to pour all his heart's pain into his sighs.

original: یوں تیرے غم میں گزرے ہیں لمحات میرے
دیکھ کے پریشان تبسم کو بھی رونا آیا
transliteration: Yoon tere gham mein guzre hain lamhaat mere
Dekh ke pareshaan, Tabassum ko bhi rona aaya
translation: This is how my moments have passed, grieving for you:
seeing such distress, even Tabassum (a smile) began to cry.
couplets.story: This is how he has spent his time since the loss. Then the play on his name: 'Tabassum' means 'smile', so even the smile itself started crying.

why: Short and moving, with a clever play on the poet's own name.
prompt: How do you show grief? Do you let yourself cry?
notes: The date (16-1-86) is printed with the title.
